meta.title: The AI Energy Bubble: Biggest Opportunity or Biggest Trap?
meta.speakers: Dave Moss, Chris Camillo, Jordan Giesige
meta.thread_line: 7 threads · the power shortfall and an energy basket, Chris's Bloom thesis, the 'AI is fake' narrative, Google's AI-mode problem, Amazon into earnings, Reddit's underpriced data deals, and Take-Two's narrative shift

snapshot: Earnings split on AI power: **Vertiv** revenue +61%, orders more than doubled, stock +16%; GE Vernova posted $29B orders and a $197B backlog, raised guidance — and fell.
Morgan Stanley sees a 38 GW global AI power shortfall through 2028 — roughly 38 large nuclear reactors that don't exist.
Chris Camillo keeps loading **Bloom Energy** and calls it the biggest winner; Jordan prefers Constellation and Vistra for their nuclear PPAs; the group lands on owning an energy basket.
Chris: Google's AI mode is so successful it's eroding search monetization — the call he made a year ago while short; he prefers Amazon.
Chris holds a levered Amazon long into tonight's print but warns the market may punish a $300-350B capex guide — and deleverages live on the show.
Reddit's AI data deals ($60M Google, $70M OpenAI) were 'embarrassingly' cheap; Chris expects renewals to reprice massively and is long.
Chris cut ~75% of his Take-Two position as investors shifted from GTA 6 hype to whether AI democratizes game-making.
The 'AI is fake' crowd (Ed Zitron on Jon Stewart, Michael Burry) gets the panel's scorn; real CEOs are signing 20-year power contracts.

themes.status: HYPERSCALERS LOCKING UP POWER FOR ~20 YEARS
themes.title: A 38 GW power gap and an energy basket: Vertiv, GE Vernova, Constellation, Vistra
themes.lead: The panel's view is that electricity, not chips, is AI's binding constraint, and the cleanest way to play it is a basket of power names rather than one winner.
bullets: Earnings day split: Vertiv revenue +61%, orders more than doubled, stock **+16%**; GE Vernova $29B orders, $197B backlog and a guidance raise — and the stock went down.
Morgan Stanley: AI global power shortfall of **38 GW** through 2028 — about 38 large nuclear reactors' worth.
Jordan likes Constellation and Vistra: long-term power purchase agreements with Meta, Amazon and Microsoft, plus government loans pushing nuclear restarts alongside legacy gas.
Jordan: Vistra guiding roughly 20-30% earnings growth for 2027 after ~40% this year — 'a good boring energy trade'.
GE Vernova is sold out to 2032 on turbines; Jordan trades in and out of it. Nobody has a view on Solaris.
Chris: hyperscalers locking up electricity for 20 years means 'someone is spectacularly wrong' — he sides with the contracts being real and plans to buy some of the 'boring' names for a basket.
Jordan on natural gas prices after weather events: don't try to get alpha predicting them.

quote.text: They're making multi-decade commitments to secure power for a technology some investors are convinced is a passing bubble. So someone is spectacularly wrong here

themes.status: CHRIS ADDING · ALL THREE HOSTS OWN
themes.title: Bloom Energy: Chris's 'biggest winner' of the AI power trade
themes.lead: Chris frames Bloom as a technology company at the start of monetizing a decade of R&D, so its high P/E and negative cash flow are the point, not the problem.
bullets: Bloom fell **20%** in two days last week, then rebounded 18% in three — Chris has been 'loading up on even more'.
On-site fuel cells need only a gas pipeline — no turbine, lower noise, no grid draw — an easier sell at angry data-center town halls.
Knock: power costs a premium, but it gets cheaper every year; Chris sees it reaching parity with grid-equivalent cost plus faster ramp.
Dave (also long) worries about valuation and negative cash flow; Jordan owns it but flags it still runs on natural gas — Chris: gas 'is not going anywhere the next five years'.
Recurring short reports (the Hunterbrook scandium claim, roughly every nine months for three years) were refuted by the CEO and independent reports, per Chris.
Chris's exit trigger: large deployments failing to scale; hyperscalers take 'baby steps' because a Bloom failure would sink a whole data center, and one proven deal unlocks the rest.

quote.text: I think bloom is probably the biggest winner here

themes.watch: All three hosts hold Bloom, and Chris is actively adding — the bull case comes from owners.

themes.title: The 'AI is fake' narrative and the misinformation trade
themes.lead: Chris argues the bubble crowd confuses circular financing and slow enterprise adoption with fake demand, and that uncorrected viral stories make short-term trading irrational.
bullets: Trigger: a viral Jon Stewart clip with Ed Zitron arguing AI demand is circular, fabricated revenue; Chris says the bear 'bar moves every 60 to 90 days'.
Chris: 'finance by its nature is circular' — the test is whether end-user value exceeds spend, and that isn't supposed to happen on day one.
CRM analogy: firms spent up to two years onboarding Salesforce and another year before staff used it right — AI adoption is 'a multi-decade journey'.
Jordan: companies use AI in silos that mirror today's org chart; restructuring around it will be slow but inevitable.
Jordan cites a TikTok stock creator whose bearish videos got ~**10x** the engagement of bullish ones.
Misinformation examples: Anthropic's '$80B loss' was a mark-up of notes issued to Amazon; Google took a non-cash write-down on its SpaceX stake this quarter — Chris: '95%' never see the correction.
Chris still takes AI doom seriously: a 'meaningful tail risk' it could kill us all.

quote.text: this ed zitron guy might be the most wrong person in 30 years of watching the market

themes.status: CHRIS NOT INVESTED · CLOSED EARLIER SHORT
themes.title: Google's AI mode is succeeding so well it's eroding search economics
themes.lead: Chris's call from a year ago landed on last night's call: AI mode usage is dragging search revenue growth because it monetizes worse than classic search.
bullets: Google's earnings call showed AI mode usage negatively impacting search revenue growth — Chris: the story is AI succeeding spectacularly, not failing.
Chris shorted Google a year ago on 'faking' search growth via unmonetized AI queries, got roasted, and covered — Jordan: 'way too early'.
Search was historically ~**85%** of Google's profits; the bull case is TPUs plus cloud offsetting it — Chris would rather get that AI-infra exposure elsewhere.
Advertisers on X and Reddit say Google is squeezing every penny — Jordan points to a Max Anderson thread on exact-match keywords being broadened.
Chris: Google Trends data is now so polluted by AI queries it's 'essentially trash' for social-arbitrage research.
He'd change his view if Google monetizes AI mode as well as traditional search.

quote.text: Google's showing us that AI could be so wildly successful

names.blurb: AI mode cannibalizing search monetization; Chris not invested after covering a short

themes.status: EARNINGS AFTER HOURS OCT 29, 2026 · CHRIS LEVERED LONG
themes.title: Amazon into earnings: agentic-shopping fears overblown, capex reaction is the risk
themes.lead: Chris holds a large levered Amazon long and would buy any capex-driven sell-off, but cut options live because he doesn't trust the market to read the print rationally.
bullets: Bear worry: shopping agents erode Amazon's high-growth ad business; Chris: 'many, many years' to play out and Amazon will run its own agents.
Amazon blocks bots to keep control of the customer — unauthorized purchases mean chargebacks, returns and fraud that must be solved first.
Viewer question on Elon praising Shopify and knocking Amazon for blocking GrokBot — Chris puts eventual Amazon bot partnerships at 'close to 100' percent.
Last capex guide: **$220B** for 2026; Chris thinks $300-350B for next year is possible and the market would 'smoke' it. Microsoft is down after its report too.

Other overhangs: diesel costs for the largest logistics operation, RAM costs hitting Alexa devices; the revamped Alexa lineup includes a ~$700 16-inch counter screen, but ad-heavy devices draw complaints.
Chris trimmed options mid-show — 'deleveraging live' — warning viewers not to be over-levered short term.

quote.text: I don't have cold feet on my Amazon thesis

themes.status: EARNINGS OCT 29, 2026 · DATA DEALS UP FOR RENEWAL
themes.title: Reddit: AI is killing its traffic, but its data deals were sold for pennies
themes.lead: Chris thinks the market is fixated on falling search-driven traffic while Reddit's AI licensing contracts are set to reprice from tens of millions to potentially billions.
bullets: Reddit has been punished all year because Google AI mode and chatbots answer questions without sending visitors — 'does anyone click those little links? No.'
Licensing deals: Google's ~$60M (signed Feb 2024) and OpenAI's ~**$70M** (May 2024) — Chris calls them 'misnegotiated' and 'embarrassing'.
Chris expects renewals between Q2 and Q4 2027 to be far bigger and usage-variable, so Reddit gets paid as AI queries grow.
He calls Reddit possibly the most valuable acquisition target in the world for an AI company; Dave notes a rival's attempt to build a competitor would cost billions.
Dave: upvotes provide a validation layer, and AI can cross-check Reddit answers against other sources.
Chris is long (unlevered, no options) and 'would like to be levered' but can't time the leak; one co-host has a small underwater position, another has none.

quote.text: I could make a case that those deals should be billions.

themes.watch: Renewal timing is muddled on air: Chris says the deals end Q2-Q4 2027, while the cited signing dates imply Feb and May 2026 expiries. Chris discloses an unlevered long.

names.name: Reddit (RDDT)
names.blurb: Traffic hit by AI answers; data-licensing renewals could reprice massively

themes.title: Take-Two: the GTA 6 debate gave way to 'is there value in a game publisher in 2035?'
themes.lead: Chris cut most of his Take-Two stake once investors began pricing AI-democratized game development as an inevitability, not a near-term event.
bullets: Chris and Dave argue over 'it'll be a hit': GTA 6 is projected around 30M copies — Chris says only a runaway beat (e.g. 130M) moves the stock.
New narrative: if anyone can generate games on the fly, legacy publishers' long-dated revenue is in doubt even with 3-4 strong years left.
**Salesforce** analogy: not going away, but startups will use one of 100 cheap AI-coded rivals while American Airlines keeps the system of record — a multiple headwind.
Future of gaming may look like content creation: tens of millions of creators, tiny communities, near-free games.
Chris heard claims GTA 6 could be reverse-engineered with AI in days; Jordan is skeptical — 'the engine does a lot of work'.
Chris sold ~**75%** (keeps 20-25%): 'you have to be open to new information'.

takeaways.title: Build an AI-power basket (fuel cells, nuclear-PPA utilities, turbines) rather than betting on a single winner.
Track Bloom's large hyperscaler deployments — scaling trouble there is the thesis-breaker.
Size leveraged earnings trades for the worst case; capex guides are being punished regardless of demand.
Watch whether Google can monetize AI mode like classic search before treating it as an AI winner.
Follow Reddit's data-licensing renewals — a leaked deal sets the price for every AI lab.
Cut a position when the narrative investors care about changes, even if your original thesis is intact.

claims.claim: AI faces a global power shortfall of 38 GW through 2028.
Amazon could guide next year's capex to $300-350B, up from $220B in 2026, and the stock would sell off.
Amazon eventually partners with third-party shopping bots.
Reddit's AI data-licensing deals renew at far higher, usage-variable prices.
Bloom Energy's power cost reaches parity with equivalent grid energy over the next few years.
GTA 6 only moves Take-Two meaningfully if it far exceeds the ~30M-copy projection.

other_news.title: Chris did a 30-minute Tesla FSD demo in Friday rush hour on Dallas's 75 without touching the wheel — 'the least stressful time I've ever been behind the wheel' — and bought two Model Ys; still waiting on Optimus news.

Chris and Dave rave about a new three-hour, theaters-only film on Elizabeth Holmes from the creator of Nathan For You and The Rehearsal — avoid spoilers; Holmes' sentence was cut from 11 years 3 months to about 10.
Recommended: Tires season 3; Shane Gillis was 'canceled' over an SNL joke tied to a Tires scene.

Sources referenced: Morgan Stanley (power shortfall), a Jon Stewart / Ed Zitron interview clip, Michael Burry, a Max Anderson thread on Google ads, a Hunterbrook short report on Bloom, and a TikTok creator's engagement experiment.

glossary.def: A long-term contract to buy electricity from a producer at agreed terms — here, hyperscalers locking up power for ~20 years.
Money flowing between AI companies as investments and purchases, which bears say inflates demand.
Google's AI-answer search experience, which monetizes worse than traditional ad-driven search.
Chris's approach of trading on consumer trends spotted in social and search data before Wall Street notices.
AI agents making purchases on a consumer's behalf, raising chargeback, return and fraud issues for retailers.
